significance: A small shrine to Lakshmi abutting the south-east minaret of the Charminar in Hyderabad's old city. The structure standing today was put up in the 1960s, and historians hold that the stone it grew around was a guard stone set to protect the monument's corner from traffic.
story: Local tradition dates the stone to the Qutb Shahi period and links the shrine's name to Bhagmati, the queen after whom the city is said to have first been named.
